title: One of four British moth samples had a lower late-season warmth slope for fixed-size richness in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested the August-September minus May-June temperature slope for fixed-size moth catch richness in 506 British trap-months. Four models covered England and Scotland in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015. They controlled trap by month, rain, sampling effort and linear time. Only early England had a contrast below zero after four-test correction: -3.82 taxa per C, with interval -5.76 to -1.88. The other contrasts were -2.11, +0.47 and +3.92, with intervals that included zero. Extra effort and trend controls kept the early English result. A smaller fixed catch size gave an uncertain contrast. Scottish early-season coverage was sparse. These tests reuse a published campaign panel, which we rebuilt from public sources. Selected catches, coarse weather, few year clusters and capture bias limit inference. The results do not identify a timing mechanism or a causal climate effect. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and a figure are included. External record-level data stay outside the package.

display.caption: Late-season minus early-season warmth slopes. Bars give intervals corrected for four tests within each outcome. Only early English fixed-size richness has an interval below zero.

citations.reason: Panel code and source rules are reused. The panel was rebuilt and checked. Biological records overlap. We add a direct seasonal slope contrast.
